title: Nayaks of Madurai
capsule: The Madurai Nayak dynasty was founded around 1529 when Viswanatha Nayak was appointed governor of Madurai by the Vijayanagara emperor Achyuta Deva Raya, and it evolved into a de facto independent Telugu-Balija kingdom as Vijayanagara's power waned after the Battle of Talikota (1565). The dynasty's most celebrated ruler, Tirumala Nayaka (r. 1623–1659), rebuilt and vastly expanded the Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai and patronized Tamil and Telugu literature. Rani Mangammal served as an effective regent (1689–1706) after the death of her grandson, demonstrating the dynasty's capacity for female leadership. Vijaya Ranga Chokkanatha, the last effective ruler, died in 1731 and was succeeded by a series of contested rulers before the Nayak state was conquered by the Nawab of Arcot with Maratha assistance in 1736, ending the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's political history is well documented in Telugu, Tamil, and Dutch East India Company records; territorial boundaries of its control are approximately attested and shifted considerably over time.
